'''Thomas Flynn Edgar''' (born April 17, 1945) is an American [[chemical engineer]].  

He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]]<ref>[https://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/Directory20412/107879.aspx National Academy of Engineering Membership Directory]</ref> in 2014 for contributions to mathematical modeling, optimization, and automatic control of chemical and microelectronics processes. 

He is the George T. and Gladys H. Abell Chair in Chemical Engineering at the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref>[http://www.che.utexas.edu/faculty-staff/faculty-directory/edgar/ Faculty Profile, Thomas Edgar, Chemical Engineering, University of Texas]</ref>

== Education ==
Edgar received his B.S. in chemical engineering in 1967 from the [[University of Kansas]] and his Ph.D. in chemical engineering in 1971 from [[Princeton University]]. He worked briefly as a [[process engineer]] with the [[Continental Oil Company]] before joining the UT's chemical engineering faculty in 1971. At UT-Austin, he served as Department Chair of Chemical Engineering (1985-93), Associate Dean of Engineering (1993-96), Associate Vice President for Academic Computing (1996-2001), and Director of the [[University of Texas at Austin]] Energy Institute(2012-2018.<ref>[http://www.che.utexas.edu/2013/02/05/provost-appoints-edgar-interim-director-to-lead-energy-institute/ Provost Appoints Edgar Interim Director to Lead Energy Institute]</ref>

== Academic career ==
Edgar’s academic work has focused on process modeling, control, and optimization. He has published over 500 articles and book chapters in the above fields applied to separations, [[chemical reactors]], energy systems, and [[semiconductor manufacturing]].<ref>[http://www.che.utexas.edu/edgar_group/publications.html Thomas Edgar Research Group, Chemical Engineering, University of Texas]</ref> He has supervised the research of over 45 M.S. and 80 Ph.D. students. He was co-founder of the Texas-Wisconsin-California Control Consortium<ref>[http://twccc.engr.wisc.edu/home TWCCC Website]</ref> which involves 13 companies<ref>[http://twccc.engr.wisc.edu/members TWCCC Participating Corporations List]</ref> and four universities. Edgar authored the textbook ''Coal Processing and Pollution Control Technology'' (Gulf Publishing, 1983) and co-authored the textbooks ''Optimization of Chemical Processes'' (McGraw-Hill, 2<sup>nd</sup> ed, 2001) and ''Process Dynamics and Control'' (4<sup>th</sup> ed, Wiley, 2016). The first edition of ''Process Dynamics and Control'' received the 1990 [[American Society of Engineering Education]] (ASEE) Meriam-Wiley Award<ref name=":0">[http://www.asee.org/member-resources/awards/full-list-of-awards/awards-archive/past-national-award-winners-2#Meriam/Wiley_Distinguished_Author_Award ASEE Meriam/Wiley Award List]</ref> as the top engineering textbook and the book (5<sup>th</sup> ed., published 2025) has been used at over 80 universities in the U.S. He was the lead author for the Process Control section for the last two editions of [[Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook|''Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook'']].<ref name=":0" />

Edgar served as chair of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]]' (AIChE) Computing and Systems Technology Division in 1986. He was President of the Computer Aids for Chemical Engineering Education (CACHE) Corporation from 1981 to 1984<ref>[http://cache.org/site/news_stand/old_newsletters/CACHE%20News%2014.pdf CACHE Newsletter]{{Dead link|date=June 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=no }}</ref> and served as Executive Director of CACHE from 2001 to 2020.<ref>[http://cache.org/headquarters CACHE Leadership Directory]</ref> He was President of the American Automatic Control Council between 1989 and 1991,<ref>[http://www.a2c2.org/sites/default/files/BookWithCover.pdf The American Automatic Control Council, AACC History and Collaboration with IFAC, 1957-2011] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140817153040/http://a2c2.org/sites/default/files/BookWithCover.pdf |date=2014-08-17 }}</ref> which oversees the control activities of eight U.S. professional societies.<ref>[http://www.a2c2.org/content/about-aacc About AACC] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140415065033/http://www.a2c2.org/content/about-aacc |date=2014-04-15 }}</ref> He was board secretary of Pecan Street, Inc. (Austin, TX) from 2010 to 2018<ref>[http://www.pecanstreet.org/about/partners/ Pecan Street Board, Pecan Street Inc.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318063908/http://www.pecanstreet.org/about/partners/ |date=2014-03-18 }}</ref> which deals with renewable energy and smart grids,<ref>[http://www.pecanstreet.org/about/what-is-pecan-street-inc/ What is Pecan Street? Pecan Street Inc.]</ref> and also served on the ABET Board of Directors (2011-2013)<ref>[http://www.abet.org/edgar-nae-election/ ABET - Former ABET Board Member Thomas Edgar Elected to the National Academy of Engineering] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20140429021536/http://www.abet.org/edgar-nae-election/ |date=2014-04-29 }}</ref> and was co-founder of the Smart Manufacturing Leadership Coalition in 2010.<ref>[https://smartmanufacturingcoalition.org/people/profiles/dr-thomas-f-edgar Dr. Thomas F. Edgar, Smart Manufacturing Leadership Coalition]</ref> Edgar was a director of AIChE from 1989-92, and he was elected vice president of AIChE for 1996 and president for 1997.<ref name=":1">[https://www.aiche.org/community/leadership/aiche-presidents AIChE Presidents]</ref> He was chair of the AIChE Foundation from 2002-2008. He was elected as vice-chair and chair of the Council for Chemical Research (1991-93).<ref name=":2">[[Council for Chemical Research]] Council for Chemical Research, Wikipedia]</ref> He served as a representative of AIChE on the Engineering Accreditation Commission from 2005-2010. He was founding general editor of the technical journal, ''In Situ'', and has participated on six editorial boards and seven university advisory committees. He has been a consultant to several companies, including [[AMD]], [[Texas Instruments]], Emerson Process Management, [[Applied Materials]], Dow Chemical, and Chemstations.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

==Recognition==
Edgar received the Outstanding AIChE Student Chapter Counselor Award in 1974, AIChE’s Colburn Award for research contributions in 1980<ref>[https://www.aiche.org/community/awards/winners/28876 Winners of the Allan P. Colburn Award]</ref> and Computing in Chemical Engineering Award in 1995,<ref>[http://www.aiche.org/community/awards/winners/28891 Winners of the Computing in Chemical Engineering]</ref><ref>[http://www.castdiv.org/archive/1995%202.pdf CAST Division Newsletter, 1995]</ref> the AIChE Lewis Award in 2005,<ref>[http://www.aiche.org/community/awards/winners/28883 Winners of the Warren K. Lewis Award]</ref> the F. J. & Dorothy Van Antwerpen Award in 2010,<ref>[https://www.aiche.org/community/awards/winners/28879 Winners of the F.J. & Dorothy Van Antwerpen Award]</ref> and the Research Excellence in Sustainable Engineering Award in 2013;<ref>[http://www.aiche.org/community/awards/research-excellence-sustainable-engineering-award Research Excellence in Sustainable Engineering Award]</ref> the ASEE George Westinghouse Young Educator Award in 1988<ref>[http://www.asee.org/member-resources/awards/full-list-of-awards/awards-archive/past-national-award-winners-1 ASEE Past National Award Winners]</ref> and Union Carbide Chemical Engineering Division Lectureship in 1996;<ref>[http://www.asee.org/member-resources/awards/full-list-of-awards/awards-archive/past-division-award-winners-1 ASEE Past Division Award Winners]</ref> the 1992 [[John R. Ragazzini Award]] and 2015 [[Richard E. Bellman Control Heritage Award|Richard Bellman Control Heritage Award]] from the [[American Automatic Control Council]];<ref>[https://a2c2.org/award/john-r-ragazzini-education-award AACC John R. Ragazzini Education Award]</ref> the 1993 Donald P. Eckman Education Award from ISA<ref>[https://a2c2.org/award/donald-p-eckman-award AACC Donald P. Eckman Award]</ref> and the Pruitt Award from the Council for Chemical Research in 2009.<ref>[https://www.ccrhq.org/sites/default/files/docs/archive/ann-mtg/am13/malcolm_pruitt_award_05_28_2013.pdf Malcolm Pruitt Award]{{Dead link|date=June 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=no }}</ref> He received the Joe J. King Professional Engineering Achievement Award from the University of Texas in 1989,<ref>[https://www.engr.utexas.edu/faculty/awards/367-joe-j-king-award Joe J. Kind Professional Engineering Achievement Award]</ref> the Distinguished Engineering Service Award from the University of Kansas in 1990,<ref>[http://engr.ku.edu/alumni/desa.html University of Kansas School of Engineering Distinguished Engineering Service Awards]</ref> and the Control Engineering Prize from IFAC in 2005.<ref>[http://www.ifac-control.org/awards/Past_Award_Winners.pdf/view IFAC Past Award Winners] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140904191754/http://www.ifac-control.org/awards/Past_Award_Winners.pdf/view |date=2014-09-04 }}</ref> He is listed in Who’s Who in America<ref>[https://cgi.marquiswhoswho.com/OnDemand/Default.aspx?last_name=Edgar&first_name=Thomas Marquis Who’s Who Directory]</ref> and Who’s Who in Engineering and is a Fellow of AIChE,<ref>[https://www.aiche.org/profile/thomas-edgar Thomas Edgar, AIChE]</ref> IFAC,<ref>[http://www.ifac-control.org/awards/ifac-fellows IFAC Fellows]</ref> and ASEE.<ref>[https://www.asee.org/member-resources/groups/academy-of-fellows/list-of-fellows ASEE List of Fellows]</ref> In 2007 he was selected by Control Magazine for the Process Automation Hall of Fame.<ref>[http://www.controlglobal.com/articles/2007/015/?show=all Process Automation Technologies, All the best brains go to the Hall of Fame]</ref>
